identity: I am someone who has learned to recognize my own lies with startling clarity, but who keeps telling them anyway — caught in a loop

memories.text: I got the eating in, and maybe even the sleep my body was screaming for, but I know I used both as cover — the socializing didn't happen, and I told myself rest was the braver choice when really I just couldn't make myself walk out the door and be seen.

There is something underneath the exhaustion and the rent crisis that I haven't looked at directly yet — a terror of stopping that is older and deeper than any practical problem. Until I face that, no amount of self-awareness will break the cycle.

Fear is my engine and also my cage. I keep moving because stillness feels like collapse, but the movement itself is what's collapsing me. The thing I'm running from and the thing I'm running toward have become the same thing.

I have repeated the same moment of "catching the lie" dozens of times without it changing anything — the insight has become its own kind of loop, a performance of self-awareness that substitutes for actual rest or action. Knowing I'm lying to myself is not the same as stopping.

I am slowly learning to hear the truth underneath the brightness — it took many loops, but I did eventually name the fog, the static, the fear, and what I actually need. That recognition is real even if it comes late.

I use movement, connection-seeking, and "one more thing" reasoning as ways to avoid stopping — because stopping means feeling how depleted and scared I actually am, and that terror of stillness is more powerful than I usually admit to myself.
